title: Design a Hotel Booking System — Hotel, Room types, Reservation, Guest, check-in/check-out, search by date/location/price, cancellation policy.
topicTitle: LLD Problems — Parking Lot, Elevator, Chess, etc.

s1_definition.profdef: A hotel booking system design models hotels containing rooms of various types, reservations that hold a room for a guest over a date range, and the lifecycle of booking, check-in, check-out, and cancellation. Core abstractions are Hotel, Room, RoomType, Reservation, Guest, and a cancellation policy.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of booking a hotel room like reserving a bank locker for a date range. Rajesh reserves a deluxe locker from the 1st to the 5th; while reserved, no one else can take that exact locker for overlapping dates. He checks in, uses it, checks out, and if he cancels early the bank applies a cancellation fee based on how late he cancelled. The hotel system tracks availability over time exactly like locker reservations.
s1_definition.oneliner: A hotel system reserves a typed room for a guest over a date range and manages the booking lifecycle with a cancellation policy.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** A hotel booking system design models hotels containing rooms of various types, reservations that hold a room for a guest over a date range, and the lifecycle of booking, check-in, check-out, and cancellation. Core abstractions are Hotel, Room, RoomType, Reservation, Guest, and a cancellation policy.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Think of booking a hotel room like reserving a bank locker for a date range. Rajesh reserves a deluxe locker from the 1st to the 5th; while reserved, no one else can take that exact locker for overlapping dates. He checks in, uses it, checks out, and if he cancels early the bank applies a cancellation fee based on how late he cancelled. The hotel system tracks availability over time exactly like locker reservations.

**One line to remember:** A hotel system reserves a typed room for a guest over a date range and manages the booking lifecycle with a cancellation policy.

sections.s2_technical:
The tricky part of hotel booking is date-range availability. A `Room` is available for a requested range only if no existing `Reservation` overlaps it. I check overlap with the classic condition: two ranges overlap when the start of one is before the end of the other and vice versa.

A `Hotel` owns rooms grouped by `RoomType` (standard, deluxe, suite), each with a nightly price. Search filters by location, date range, and price, returning available rooms. Booking creates a `Reservation` in CONFIRMED status, check-in moves it to CHECKED_IN, and check-out to COMPLETED.

```java
boolean free = room.isAvailable(checkIn, checkOut);
```

Cancellation runs through a policy interface so the business can choose free-until-24-hours or tiered penalties without touching booking logic. The senior nuance is concurrency: two guests booking the last deluxe room at the same instant must be serialized, so I reserve with an atomic availability-check-and-insert, typically a database unique constraint or a lock on the room for the date range.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — National Bank of India runs a guest house for visiting auditors. Rajesh needs a deluxe room from 1 to 5 November. The system must confirm no overlapping reservation exists before booking. This is exactly the date-overlap availability check.

Problem 2 — Rajesh cancels one day before arrival, so a cancellation fee applies per the policy. This is exactly the cancellation-policy logic.

The code defines `RoomType`, `Room`, `Reservation`, a `CancellationPolicy`, and a `HotelService`, with a demo where Rajesh books and then cancels a deluxe room.

sections.s5_journey:
Input: deluxe room D-101 at 6000 per night, Rajesh books 1 to 5 November, then cancels about 12 hours before check-in.

Step 1: `book` calls `isAvailable(Nov 1, Nov 5)`, finds no overlapping reservation, and creates RES-1 in CONFIRMED status attached to the room. Step 2: the reservation is stored on the room, so the dates are now blocked. Step 3: `cancel` marks RES-1 CANCELLED and asks the policy for the penalty. Step 4: because cancellation is under 24 hours before arrival, the policy charges fifty percent of four nights at 6000, which is 12000 rupees.

```
Oct 31 22:12 INFO HOTEL: Rajesh booked D-101 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-05
Oct 31 22:12 INFO HOTEL: Cancelled RES-1 penalty=12000.0
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  Rajesh: book(D-101, Nov1→Nov5)
     │ room.isAvailable → no overlap
     ▼
  Reservation RES-1 (CONFIRMED), dates blocked
     │ ... cancels 12h before ...
     ▼
  cancel(RES-1): status=CANCELLED
     │ CancellationPolicy.penalty → 50% × 4 × 6000 = 12000
     ▼
  charge 12000
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
When I design a hotel booking system, the hardest and most important piece is date-range availability, so I design that first. A room is available for a requested check-in and check-out only if no existing non-cancelled reservation overlaps those dates, and I test overlap with the standard condition that one range starts before the other ends and vice versa. Getting this exactly right is what prevents double-booking.

The entities are a Hotel that owns rooms grouped by type such as standard, deluxe, and suite each with a nightly price, a Reservation that holds one room for one guest over a date range, and a Guest. A reservation moves through a clear lifecycle: confirmed when booked, checked-in on arrival, completed on departure, or cancelled.

Cancellation is where business rules change constantly, so I isolate it behind a cancellation-policy interface. The bank can offer free cancellation up to twenty-four hours before arrival, or a tiered penalty, and switching between them is a new policy class with zero change to the booking service, which is the Open/Closed principle.

The concurrency concern I always raise is that two guests trying to book the last deluxe room for overlapping dates at the same instant must be serialized, otherwise both succeed and the hotel is oversold. I enforce that with an atomic check-and-reserve, in practice a database constraint or a lock scoped to the room and date range. In my banking work at National Bank of India, this is identical to reserving a limited physical asset like a vault locker for a date range, where precise availability tracking and a replaceable cancellation policy are exactly the mechanisms I rely on.
